items.title: South Africa’s Rand Faces Bleak August as Policy Stance Queried
items.description: August is historically the rand’s worst month, and traders expect this year to be no different as questions about the central bank’s policy stance add to seasonal woes for South Africa’s currency.

items.title: UK’s Markets Regulator Unveils Scope of Data Feed for Stocks
items.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority unveiled how much data it will allow to be published on UK equities trading on Friday, a move that could encourage more activity on the London Stock Exchange.

items.title: Foreign Investors Shun Nigeria’s World-Beating Equities
items.description: Foreign investors shunned Nigerian stocks this year, choosing to focus on fixed-income assets, missing out on a 66% rally that made the market the world’s best performer.

items.title: Dollar Heads for Worst Week in Three Months as Fed Doubts Grow
items.description: The dollar headed for its worst week in three months on concerns the Federal Reserve won’t move forcefully enough to contain inflation.

items.description: BP Plc said it’s starting a process to market its North Sea business for a potential sale, as part of a wider review of the oil major’s portfolio.

items.title: Saudi Ships Shun Red Sea Chokepoint for Rare Africa Journey
items.description: Six Saudi oil tankers are sailing away from the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint and appeared to be embarking on an unusual trip around Africa as threats from Houthi rebels upend shipping in the Red Sea.
